title: Sample the full spatial equilibrium law in complete binary time
statement: Use accepted DDB1 at activities Wc and the actual aggregate class to sample totals. Given each species total M, allocate its counts sequentially across n sites using O(n) binomial draws: among k>=2 remaining sites call the fixed two-species A<->B class of total M with positive activities(1,k-1), giving Binomial(M,1/k); the final site receives the remainder. Adaptive unconditional TV budgets sum to epsilon across O(dn) calls. Every output placement lies in the actual spatial class, and its entire law is TV-accurate. All variable inputs, graph validation, dn binary count outputs, finite preprocessing and random bits have polynomial complete-binary cost. At n=1 no allocation is needed. This avoids per-particle enumeration and a free growing-dimensional counting oracle.
